standard_prerequisites.name: Square-full divisors
standard_prerequisites.statement: s(n) denotes the largest square-full divisor of n, and n = n^flat * s(n) with n^flat the square-free part.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof splits n as a * b with b = s(n) at source line 529 and then sums over square-full b.

standard_prerequisites.name: Divisor-summation and partial sums of a power
standard_prerequisites.statement: Partial sums of a^{-alpha} for alpha < 1 grow like (x/b)^{1-alpha}.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the bound applied at source lines 531-532 to the inner sum over a.

standard_prerequisites.name: Convergence of the square-full series
standard_prerequisites.statement: The series over square-full b of b^{beta-1} converges when beta < 1/2, since the square-full numbers have density of order x^{1/2}.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is exactly the assumption beta < 1/2 used at source line 536 to close the estimate.

core_obligations: Rewrite the expectation as the tail sum S = sum over n <= x of (x/n)^alpha s(n)^beta, so that the goal becomes S << x (source lines 525-528).
Split n as a * b with b = s(n) square-full and a = n^flat, and bound S by a double sum over b and a <= x/b (source lines 529-531).
Bound the inner sum over a by (x/b)^{1-alpha}, which uses alpha < 1, and recognise that the b^{beta-alpha} factor then cancels against it to leave x * b^{beta-1} (source lines 532-533).
Conclude by the convergence of the sum of b^{beta-1} over square-full b, which is where the hypothesis beta < 1/2 enters (source lines 534-536).

proof_roadmap.step: Turn the expectation into the tail sum S and split each n by its square-full divisor.
Double-count over b and a, bound the inner sum by (x/b)^{1-alpha} and cancel the powers.
Close with the convergence of the square-full series under beta < 1/2.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:properties of N` at source lines 517-523: for fixed alpha in [0,1) and beta in [0,1/2) the quantity E[(x/N_x)^alpha s(N_x)^beta] is bounded uniformly in x. The author's proof (source lines 525-537) replaces the probabilistic statement by the tail sum S over n <= x of (x/n)^alpha s(n)^beta (lines 526-528), then performs an explicit divisor decomposition n = a*b with b = s(n) square-full (line 529), an inner partial-sum estimate that consumes alpha < 1 (lines 531-532), a cancellation of powers of b (line 533) and finally a convergence argument for the square-full series that consumes beta < 1/2 (lines 535-536). The two parameter hypotheses are used at two different places, and neither the decomposition nor the cancellation is indicated by the statement.
